title: XRPH Wallet wallet-generation root-cause disclosure
notes: Adds the subsequently disclosed and independently reproduced wallet-generation entropy defect as a distinct lifecycle/security event. This does not replace wlr_ev_000246: the previously recorded staking/backend seed-transmission finding remains a separate architecture issue and is not treated as the root cause for the full victim population. Canonical IDs are provisional until promotion from fresh main.

events.title: Wallet-generation entropy defect identified as XRPH Wallet drain root cause
events.description: XRP Healthcare published developer findings identifying a reproducible defect in XRPH Wallet's app-specific wallet-generation flow: improperly formatted app-generated entropy was passed into the XRPL key-generation path, sharply reducing the effective private-key search space and making offline reconstruction computationally feasible. Independent public forensic review reproduced the weak app-created wallet-generation mechanics and measured the effective search space at roughly 2^46.
events.notes: The vendor's published root-cause finding and independent reproduction support the weak-entropy mechanism. This event is deliberately separate from wlr_ev_000246: observed seed transmission in staking/unstaking and other backend-connected flows remains a material architecture finding, but is not required to explain the full 4,010-victim population. The record does not infer who exploited the weakness, the attacker's hardware, or an exact key-discovery timeline.

evidence.title: XRPH Wallet Root-Cause Technical Report - Developer Findings
evidence.notes: First-party developer root-cause report. XRP Healthcare's accompanying public statement says the team identified and reproduced improperly formatted entropy entering the XRPL key-generation function, reducing the effective keyspace and making offline private-key reconstruction feasible.

evidence.title: XRPH Wallet Incident: Public Forensics Report
evidence.notes: Independent public forensic review reproduces the app-specific createNewPadlock -> Wallet.fromEntropy(string) weakness, explains the string-coercion failure, estimates an effective search space of about 2^46.05, and separately preserves the backend seed-exposure finding without treating it as necessary to explain all victims.
